title.en: Experimental study of the photoelectric effect

heading.en: Turning the knobs of a photocell

hook.en: In a photocell we can change three things: the brightness of the light, its colour, and the voltage. Each tells us something surprising about light.
hook.kn: ದ್ಯುತಿಕೋಶದಲ್ಲಿ ಮೂರು ವಿಷಯಗಳನ್ನು ಬದಲಾಯಿಸಬಹುದು: ಬೆಳಕಿನ ತೀವ್ರತೆ, ಅದರ ಬಣ್ಣ (ಆವೃತ್ತಿ) ಮತ್ತು ವೋಲ್ಟೇಜ್. ಪ್ರತಿಯೊಂದೂ ಬೆಳಕಿನ ಬಗ್ಗೆ ಅಚ್ಚರಿಯ ಸಂಗತಿ ಹೇಳುತ್ತದೆ.

title.en: Describe the effect of intensity, potential and frequency
Define stopping potential and threshold frequency

say.en: In a photocell we can change three things: the brightness of the light, its colour, and the voltage. Each tells us something surprising about light. In this lesson: Describe the effect of intensity, potential and frequency.
Define stopping potential and threshold frequency.

body.en: The photocurrent is proportional to the *intensity* of light. As the collector is made more positive the current rises to a saturation value. Making the collector negative reduces the current; at the stopping potential $V_0$ even the fastest electrons are stopped, so $K_{max} = eV_0$. For a given frequency, $V_0$ is the same for all intensities.
body.kn: ದ್ಯುತಿಪ್ರವಾಹವು ಬೆಳಕಿನ ತೀವ್ರತೆಗೆ ಅನುಪಾತೀಯ. ನಿಲುಗಡೆ ವಿಭವ V₀ ನಲ್ಲಿ ವೇಗದ ಎಲೆಕ್ಟ್ರಾನ್‌ಗಳೂ ನಿಲ್ಲುತ್ತವೆ: K_max = eV₀. V₀ ತೀವ್ರತೆಯನ್ನು ಅವಲಂಬಿಸುವುದಿಲ್ಲ.

say.en: The photocurrent is proportional to the intensity of light. As the collector is made more positive the current rises to a saturation value. Making the collector negative reduces the current; at the stopping potential V 0 even the fastest electrons are stopped, so K max equals eV 0. For a given frequency, V 0 is the same for all intensities. Saturation current is proportional to intensity.
say.kn: ದ್ಯುತಿಪ್ರವಾಹವು ಬೆಳಕಿನ ತೀವ್ರತೆಗೆ ಅನುಪಾತೀಯ. ನಿಲುಗಡೆ ವಿಭವ V 0 ನಲ್ಲಿ ವೇಗದ ಎಲೆಕ್ಟ್ರಾನ್‌ಗಳೂ ನಿಲ್ಲುತ್ತವೆ: K max equals eV 0. V 0 ತೀವ್ರತೆಯನ್ನು ಅವಲಂಬಿಸುವುದಿಲ್ಲ.

say.en: K max equals eV 0.
V 0 independent of intensity.

narration.en: Let us draw Lenard's apparatus and the graphs it gives.

say.en: In an evacuated tube, light falls on the emitter plate C. Electrons fly to the collector A, and the ammeter shows a photocurrent. The battery can be reversed.
Current against potential: brighter light gives a bigger saturation current, but the current stops at the same stopping potential.
Higher frequency gives a larger stopping potential. Below a threshold frequency there is no emission at all.
The stopping potential measures the fastest electrons: K_max = eV₀. A stopping potential of 1.5 V means K_max = 1.5 eV. And emission starts with no time lag.
Let us draw Lenard's apparatus and the graphs it gives.

narration.en: Drag the yellow point to set the anode potential. With a large positive potential every emitted electron is collected: the saturation current, which grows with intensity. Make the anode negative and only fast electrons get through; at −V0 the current stops. V0 depends on frequency, not intensity. (Simplified straight-line model.)

caption.en: Drag the yellow point to set the anode potential. With a large positive potential every emitted electron is collected: the saturation current, which grows with intensity. Make the anode negative and only fast electrons get through; at −V0 the current stops. V0 depends on frequency, not intensity. (Simplified straight-line model.)
caption.kn: ಆನೋಡ್ ವಿಭವ ಹೊಂದಿಸಲು ಹಳದಿ ಬಿಂದು ಎಳೆಯಿರಿ. ಹೆಚ್ಚು ಧನ ವಿಭವದಲ್ಲಿ ಎಲ್ಲ ಎಲೆಕ್ಟ್ರಾನ್ ಸಂಗ್ರಹ: ಸಂತೃಪ್ತ ಪ್ರವಾಹ, ತೀವ್ರತೆಯೊಂದಿಗೆ ಹೆಚ್ಚುತ್ತದೆ. ಆನೋಡ್ ಋಣ ಮಾಡಿದರೆ ವೇಗದ ಎಲೆಕ್ಟ್ರಾನ್ ಮಾತ್ರ; −V0 ನಲ್ಲಿ ಪ್ರವಾಹ ನಿಲ್ಲುತ್ತದೆ. V0 ಆವೃತ್ತಿಯನ್ನು ಅವಲಂಬಿಸುತ್ತದೆ, ತೀವ್ರತೆಯನ್ನಲ್ಲ.

body.en: The stopping potential increases linearly with *frequency*. Below a threshold frequency $\nu_0$, characteristic of the metal, no electrons come out however intense the light. Above it, emission begins instantly, within about $10^{-9}$ s, even in dim light.
body.kn: ನಿಲುಗಡೆ ವಿಭವ ಆವೃತ್ತಿಯೊಂದಿಗೆ ರೇಖೀಯವಾಗಿ ಹೆಚ್ಚುತ್ತದೆ. ಆರಂಭಿಕ ಆವೃತ್ತಿ ν₀ ಗಿಂತ ಕಡಿಮೆ ಆವೃತ್ತಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಉತ್ಸರ್ಜನೆ ಇಲ್ಲ. ಉತ್ಸರ್ಜನೆ ತಕ್ಷಣ ಆಗುತ್ತದೆ.

problem.en: In a photocell the photocurrent just stops when the collector is at −1.5 V. Find the maximum kinetic energy of the photoelectrons.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. In a photocell the photocurrent just stops when the collector is at −1.5 V. Find the maximum kinetic energy of the photoelectrons.

say.en: Let us solve this together. In a photocell the photocurrent just stops when the collector is at minus 1.5 volts. Find the maximum kinetic energy of the photoelectrons.
K max equals eV 0.
K max equals 1.5 electron volts equals 1.5 times 1.6 times 10 to the power minus 19 equals 2.4 times 10 to the power minus 19 joules.
So the answer is 1.5 electron volts equals 2.4 times 10 to the power minus 19 joules.
